review_notes:
I read all of Defs.lean and grepped the DistanceGeometry directory for uses of sqDistMatrix, IsSqDistMatrix and centeredGram. I did not open the Mathlib sources, so I did not check for competing simp lemmas on `dist _ ^ 2` in EuclideanSpace. The file has two simp lemmas, `sqDistMatrix_apply` and `centeredGram_apply`. Both are `rfl` entry-wise unfoldings of a definition. They go from the opaque definition to its explicit form and cannot loop, because the right-hand sides contain neither definition.

`centeredGram_apply` unfolds to `(D 0 i + D 0 j - D i j) / 2`. This is the intended normal form. Callers either use `simp only [centeredGram_apply]` (SchoenbergHard.lean:226 and Defs.lean:132) or rewrite explicitly with `centeredGram_apply_eq_inner`. The uses in CayleyMengerVolume.lean:188–190 (`simp [centeredGram_apply, h11]`) pass the lemma explicitly, so it is redundant there, but that is harmless. I found no use where a simp call is hurt by the expansion.

`sqDistMatrix` is not used outside Defs.lean, so I saw no downstream simp problem for it.

The remaining lemmas (`IsSqDistMatrix.symm`, `.hollow`, `.eq_sqDistMatrix`, `IsPreDistMatrix.*`, `centeredGram_symm`) are predicate-projection or hypothesis-carrying facts. Simp attributes on them would be unsuitable or unneeded, so I did not recommend any.

Uncertainty: I did not confirm which Mathlib simp lemmas fire on `dist _ ^ 2` in EuclideanSpace, and I cannot run Lean to test.
